definition: Propitious means favorable; showing signs that something about to be attempted is likely to succeed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word propitious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know propitious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With calm winds and a rising tide, the harbor master declared it a propitious morning for the young crew's first sail.
A suitable time merely works well enough, while a propitious time actively favors success, with the signs lining up in your favor.
Propitious conditions favor a good outcome, but a providential event seems almost heaven-sent, arriving exactly when it is needed most.

Favorable means giving a good chance of success, and it covers anything that helps — favorable odds, favorable reviews, a favorable wind. Propitious is grander and more forward-looking: the signs themselves seem to line up, promising success for what is about to be attempted. A forecast is favorable; the morning of the launch feels propitious.

Auspicious means showing signs of future success, and it is the word for beginnings — an auspicious debut, an auspicious start. Propitious describes the conditions around an attempt: a propitious moment or season favors whatever is about to be tried, beginning or not. A first concert is auspicious; a third straight week of calm seas is propitious for the crossing.
showing signs of likely failure
suggesting that something bad is coming

Latin propitius described a god who was gracious — smiling on you instead of scowling. Ancient sailors offered gifts to propitiate the sea gods: to calm their anger and get them on your side before a voyage. A propitious wind was the sign that it had worked.

A pastry chef had dreamed of opening her own shop for years.
One spring, everything lined up at once: her lease buyout came through, a busy farmers market relocated to the block she liked, and the city announced a grant program for first-time food businesses.
Reading these signs, she judged the moment propitious and signed the papers that same week.
Every sign pointed toward success for the venture she was about to attempt, which is exactly what a propitious moment is.
Propitious describes conditions or timing that favor something about to be attempted (a propitious moment, propitious weather).

Keep it distinct from fortuitous: a propitious sign points forward toward likely success, while a fortuitous event is simply a lucky accident that already happened, with no omen-like promise about what comes next.
